- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent prices are rising.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); add 2–5% buffer to forecast for such periods.
- Model overestimates in early forecast horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply downward correction for first 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply upward bias for next 5 days unless sentiment turns negative.
